title: Serving Tier Evolution: Consumption, Migration, and Pricing Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines an operationally actionable approach for evolving Redwood Inference serving tiers over the next 12–18 months. It combines product strategy (tier definitions, pricing signals), migration mechanics (customer-facing plans and engineering rollout steps), and operational guardrails (SLOs, capacity commitments, monitoring) to keep customer applications stable while improving cost-to-serve and unit economics.

Goals:

- Reduce hosted per-token cost for high-throughput customers by 18–25% through tier consolidation, predictable bundles, and improved batching defaults.
- Provide a low-friction migration path for customers to move between tiers with clear billing, SLO, and tooling guarantees.
- Minimize churn and support overhead during changes by offering canary windows, opt-in accelerators, and automatic fallbacks.

Context and drivers:

1) Market: customers increasingly require predictable monthly ocost commitments tied to SLOs rather than pure burst pricing.
2) Platform: recent runtime optimizations (KV cache improvements, quantization recommendations) enable new cost bands with minimal quality regressions.
3) Sales: enterprise customers ask for clearer upgrade/migration policy between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

Guiding principles:

- Backwards compatibility: any tier change must preserve API, response semantics, and existing client SDK contracts.
- Observable economics: customers must be able to see the cost impact of tier changes in the Console before committing.
- Safe rollout: production changes must include automated fallback to prior tier variants when latency or error budgets are violated.
- Migration symmetry: every upward move (to higher capacity or lower latency tier) must have a symmetric downgrade path.

Tier definitions (canonical):

We define three consumer-facing serving tiers that map to internal capacity and routing policies. Table below is illustrative — concrete numeric bands will be assigned per-region in the pricing exercise.

| Tier name | Target customer profile | Key guarantees | Typical use cases | Commitment model |
|-----------|------------------------|----------------|-------------------|------------------|
| Standard | Startups, dev & test | < 500ms median, best-effort batching | Chatbots, dev APIs, prototypes | Pay-as-you-go or monthly credits |
| Predictable | Mid-market apps with steady throughput | 95th pct latency SLO, 10% cost discount vs Standard | SaaS features, background generations | 3–12 month creditized commitments with rollover |
| Enterprise Dedicated | High-throughput, regulated workloads | Latency & availability SLAs (SLA credits), network isolation | Legal/financial production services | Reserved capacity (monthly/annual), optional on-prem packaging |

Migration strategy and timeline (12 months):

1. Q1 — Pilot: select 8 existing Predictable and 3 Enterprise customers to participate in an early migration pilot. Collect telemetry (latency, cost per 1M tokens, error rates) and customer qualitative feedback.
2. Q2 — Console tools: ship an in-Console migration preview that simulates 30/60/90-day cost and SLO implications and exposes a one-click scheduled migration window.
3. Q3 — Opt-in accelerator: automated batching/quantization recommendations for customers that accept migration; include a reversible rollout that can be reverted within 24 hours.
4. Q4 — Broad rollout: new sign-ups default to the updated tier map; legacy customers receive a multi-month campaign with optional incentives to migrate.

Rollout playbook (engineering + customer success):

- Pre-rollout checklist (owner: product + eng-platform):
  - Confirm telemetry instrumentation: per-route token counts, model variant mapping, latency percentiles, KV cache hit-rate.
  - Capacity safety nets: ensure fallback routes and variant compatibility exist for top 20 routes by traffic.
  - Billing simulation: generate per-customer cost delta reports for the past 90 days.

- Migration run steps (customer success lead):
  1. Run Console migration preview with customer and share simulated bill.
  2. Schedule migration window (2–4 hours low-traffic).
  3. Enable staging route on Predictable/Enterprise variant and run 5% traffic for 48 hours.
  4. If errors or latency SLOs exceed thresholds, automatically revert and open an incident (see incident template below).
  5. Post-migration: 30-day quality check and credit reconciliation.

CLI / API examples (for engineering ops):

# Preview migration for route
redwood migrate-preview --route-id r_12345 --target-tier predictable --lookback 90

# Schedule migration window
redwood migrate-schedule --route-id r_12345 --target-tier predictable --start 2026-06-14T00:00:00Z --duration 4h

Pricing and packaging considerations:

- Commitment tiers must be creditized: customers pre-pay for a bundle of tokens and receive preferential routing and burst retention.
- Flexible rollover: unused committed tokens roll into a six-month buffer to reduce churn/complaints at quarter boundaries.
- Add-on: latency buffer entitlement for Enterprise customers that receive automatic rerouting to higher-cost variants if SLOs are in danger.

Sample customer scenarios (illustrative):

| Customer profile | Current spend | Migration offer | Expected delta (monthly) | Notes |
|------------------|---------------|-----------------|-------------------------|-------|
| Growth SaaS | $25k | Move to Predictable with 6mo credits | -12% | Reduced per-token cost, small config change
| AI-native startup | $2k | Stay Standard + optimize batching | -18% | No commitment required
| Regulated fintech | $120k | Enterprise Dedicated reserved capacity | +5% (but stable) | SLA + isolation required

SLOs, monitoring, and rollback triggers:

- Tier-level SLOs (examples):
  - Standard: 95% requests < 800ms, availability 99.5%
  - Predictable: 95% requests < 500ms, availability 99.8%
  - Enterprise Dedicated: 99% requests < 350ms, availability 99.95%

- Rollback triggers (auto):
  - 5xx rate increases > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 30 minutes.
  - P50/P95 latency regression exceeding tier SLO by > 30% for 30 minutes.
  - KV cache hit-rate drop > 20% resulting in >5% token-cost increase.

Ownership and approvals:

- Product: Aisha Patel (owner) — product direction and migration policy.
- Eng-Platform: Daniel Kim — migration tooling, traffic shaping, rollout automation.
- Eng-SRE: Marina Kuznetsova — SLO definitions, rollback automation, incident playbook.
- Sales & CS: assigned AE/CSM per customer — commercial negotiation and scheduling.

Risk register and mitigations:

- Risk: Unexpected quality regressions after applying quantization or batching optimizations.
  - Mitigation: Canary at 5–10% traffic with automated quality-eval checks; require manual opt-in for hallucination-sensitive routes.
- Risk: Billing disputes due to opaque cost simulations.
  - Mitigation: Provide downloadable cost-simulation spreadsheets and a 30-day window for credits/reconciliation.
- Risk: Capacity contention during major migrations.
  - Mitigation: Stagger migrations by region and use a dynamic token-admission policy to protect legacy routes.

Incident template (to be used if rollback is triggered):

1. Summary: one-line description (e.g., "Predictable migration r_12345 reverted due to latency spike").
2. Start time / end time.
3. Impacted customers and routes.
4. Immediate mitigation: rollback to previous tier variant.
5. Data collected: traces, p50/p95/p99 latency, error traces, KV cache metrics.
4. Postmortem owner and timeline for mitigation.

Communications and GTM:

- Messaging pillars: clarity (cost & SLO effects), control (Console preview + opt-in), safety (rollbacks & credits).
- Customer comms cadence: pre-announce (8 weeks), migration invite (4 weeks), migration reminder (7 days, 48 hours, 4 hours), post-migration survey (7 days, 30 days).
- Sales enablement: one-pager playbook with sample scripts, objection handling, and a calculator for conversion economics.

Appendix: Console UX notes and data exports:

- Migration preview must show: current bucketed token consumption, simulated post-migration latency distribution, 30/60/90 day cost projection, and a downloadable CSV containing per-route deltas.
- Telemetry export columns: route_id, route_name, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hit_rate, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, errors_5xx, time_window_start.

Next steps / decisions required:

- Approve numeric pricing bands for Predictable and Enterprise tiers per-region (finance + pricing).
- Sign-off on the rollback triggers and automatic revert windows (eng-sre + legal).
- Pilot customer list and incentive packages (sales + customer success).
